World AIDS Day.fact: World AIDS Day, designated on 1 December every year since 1988, is an international day dedicated to raising awareness of the AIDS pandemic caused by the spread of HIV infection and mourning those who have died of the disease. World Milk Day.fact: == History == World Milk Day was first designated by the FAO in 2001.  June 1 was chosen as the date because many countries were already celebrating a milk day during that time of year.  The Day provides an opportunity to focus attention on milk and raise awareness of dairy’s part in healthy diets, responsible food production, and supporting livelihoods and communities.  This is supported by FAO data showing that more than one billion people's livelihoods are supported by the dairy sector and that dairy is consumed by more than six billion people globally.  The fact that many countries choose to do this on the same day lends additional importance to individual national celebrations and shows that milk is a global food.  === World Milk Day celebrations === World Milk Day 2016 In 2016, World Milk Day was celebrated in over 40 countries.  Activities included marathons and family runs, milking demonstrations and farm visits, school-based activities, concerts, conferences and seminars, competitions and a range of events focusing on promoting the value of milk and illustrating the important role played by the dairy industry in the national economy

This study thus makes Jewish mysticism accessible and tangible, so that it inspires emotional dveikus (cleaving to God) and embeds a deep spiritual element in daily Jewish life; it thereby serves a similar purpose to mussar, but through different means and with different contributions to intellectual and emotional life.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: Hasidic yeshivot study the mystical, spiritual works of Hasidic philosophy (_____)
Yeshiva.fact: Hasidic yeshivot study the mystical, spiritual works of Hasidic philosophy (Chassidus).

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: These draw on the earlier esoteric theology of _____, but articulates it in terms of inner psychological awareness and personal analogies
Yeshiva.fact: These draw on the earlier esoteric theology of Kabbalah, but articulates it in terms of inner psychological awareness and personal analogies.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: Chabad yeshivot, for example, study the Tanya, the _____, and the voluminous works of the Rebbes of Chabad for an hour and a half each morning, before prayers, and an hour and a half in the evening
Yeshiva.fact: Chabad yeshivot, for example, study the Tanya, the Likutei Torah, and the voluminous works of the Rebbes of Chabad for an hour and a half each morning, before prayers, and an hour and a half in the evening.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: As mentioned, _____ yeshivot often incorporate study of selected Kabbalistic texts into their curriculum – standard texts, as well as works by Yosef Hayyim, Yehuda Fatiyah and Yaakov Chaim Sofer
Yeshiva.fact: As mentioned, Sephardi yeshivot often incorporate study of selected Kabbalistic texts into their curriculum – standard texts, as well as works by Yosef Hayyim, Yehuda Fatiyah and Yaakov Chaim Sofer. Kabbalistic sources are brought in halachik works such as Kaf Hachaim and Ben Ish Hai – and are then studied indirectly also; see Sephardic law and customs § Lurianic Kabbalah.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: Kabbalistic sources are brought in halachik works such as Kaf Hachaim and _____ – and are then studied indirectly also; see Sephardic law and customs § Lurianic Kabbalah
Yeshiva.fact: Kabbalistic sources are brought in halachik works such as Kaf Hachaim and Ben Ish Hai – and are then studied indirectly also; see Sephardic law and customs § Lurianic Kabbalah.

Yeshiva.fact: In Hesder, Religious Zionist and Modern Orthodox yeshivot, Hashkafa ("worldview") or Machshavah (Jewish philosophy generalized as "Jewish thought") is taught formally.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: The Modern Orthodox, similarly, study the works of _____, "Rav Soloveitchik"
Yeshiva.fact: The Modern Orthodox, similarly, study the works of Joseph B. Soloveitchik, "Rav Soloveitchik".

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: Hasidic philosophy and _____ are also often taught; and Maharal may have a dedicated shiur
Yeshiva.fact: Hasidic philosophy and Mussar are also often taught; and Maharal may have a dedicated shiur.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days

Yeshiva.fact: Machshava is also a focus-area of many Midrashot.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: The rest of the Tanach (_____; acronym: Torah and Nach = "Torah, Nevi'im u'Ketuvim"; "Torah, Prophets and Writings") is usually taught through high school, although less intensively
Yeshiva.fact: The rest of the Tanach (Hebrew Bible; acronym: Torah and Nach = "Torah, Nevi'im u'Ketuvim"; "Torah, Prophets and Writings") is usually taught through high school, although less intensively.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: In Yeshivot, thereafter, _____, and especially Nach, are studied less directly
Yeshiva.fact: In Yeshivot, thereafter, Chumash, and especially Nach, are studied less directly.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: Students often also study _____'s commentary, functioning in relation to Rashi here, somewhat as Tosafot above; less frequently, other commentaries from the Mikraot Gedolot edition are reviewed
Yeshiva.fact: Students often also study Ramban's commentary, functioning in relation to Rashi here, somewhat as Tosafot above; less frequently, other commentaries from the Mikraot Gedolot edition are reviewed.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: Students may similarly study Nach independently (often using the _____ commentary); usually, Tanach is not taught per se, with exceptions being the five Megilloth and Tehillim
Yeshiva.fact: Students may similarly study Nach independently (often using the Metzudos commentary); usually, Tanach is not taught per se, with exceptions being the five Megilloth and Tehillim.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: At Hesder, _____ and Modern Orthodox yeshivot, the study of Chumash and Nach continues in parallel with Talmud study
Yeshiva.fact: At Hesder, Religious Zionist and Modern Orthodox yeshivot, the study of Chumash and Nach continues in parallel with Talmud study.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: These institutions offer formal shiurim in many, if not all, of the books of Nevi'im and _____
Yeshiva.fact: These institutions offer formal shiurim in many, if not all, of the books of Nevi'im and Ketuvim.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: The commentaries by Ramban, _____, "Rabbeinu Behaye", and "Rav Hirsch" provide much philosophical content
Yeshiva.fact: The commentaries by Ramban, Abarbanel, "Rabbeinu Behaye", and "Rav Hirsch" provide much philosophical content.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: The Sefer ha-_____, although not a commentary per se, offers a systematic legal and philosophic discussion of the commandments, and is similarly studied
Yeshiva.fact: The Sefer ha-Chinuch, although not a commentary per se, offers a systematic legal and philosophic discussion of the commandments, and is similarly studied. (The related Minchat Chinuch is often referenced in legal-focused Talmud shiurim.) Intensive study of Tanach, as for Machshava, is likewise a feature of many Midrashot.

Yeshiva.subject: Important Days
Yeshiva.question: (The related _____ is often referenced in legal-focused Talmud shiurim.) Intensive study of Tanach, as for Machshava, is likewise a feature of many Midrashot
Yeshiva.fact: (The related Minchat Chinuch is often referenced in legal-focused Talmud shiurim.) Intensive study of Tanach, as for Machshava, is likewise a feature of many Midrashot.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: The _____ was Mythological Swedish and Norwegian royal dynasty.
Yngling.fact: The Ynglings were a dynasty of kings, first in Sweden and later in Norway, primarily attested through the poem Ynglingatal. When Beowulf and Ynglingatal were composed sometime in the eighth to tenth centuries, their respective authors (scops and skalds) expected their audience to have a great deal of background information about these kings, which is shown in the allusiveness of the references.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: The dynasty also appears as _____ (Old English: Scylfingas, Old Norse: Skilfingar) in Beowulf
Yngling.fact: The dynasty also appears as Scylfings (Old English: Scylfingas, Old Norse: Skilfingar) in Beowulf.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: However, this does not tally with _____ sources
Yngling.fact: However, this does not tally with Icelandic sources.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: Several of these kings appear in _____: Eadgils (Adils), Onela (Ale), and Ohthere (Ottar Vendelkråka), but here they are called Scylfings (see the Beowulf section below)
Yngling.fact: The dynasty claimed descent from the gods Freyr and Njörðr, and other kings were likely mythical as well, whereas others may have been real: especially Egil, Ottar, Ale and Adils that are mentioned in Beowulf as well as Nordic sources. Several of these kings appear in Beowulf: Eadgils (Adils), Onela (Ale), and Ohthere (Ottar Vendelkråka), but here they are called Scylfings (see the Beowulf section below).

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: According to the _____, Nór founded Norway
Yngling.fact: According to the Orkneyinga Saga, Nór set up Norway.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: He was a direct descendant of Fornjótr, the King of "_____, Kvenland and Finnland"
Yngling.fact: He was a direct descendant of Fornjótr, the King of "Gotland, Kvenland and Finnland".

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: He is also known as _____ of Rouen, and is said to have been William the Conqueror's great-great-great-grandfather
Yngling.fact: He is also called Count Rou of Rouen, and is said to have been William the Conqueror's great-great-great-grandfather.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: Hversu Noregr byggðist ('_____ was founded') is a 14th-century account of the origin of various legendary Norwegian lineages
Yngling.fact: Hversu Noregr byggðist ('How Norway was founded') is a 14th-century account of the origin of various legendary Norwegian lineages.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: The 'genealogies' also claim that many heroic families famed in _____ tradition but not located in Norway were of a Finn-Kven stock, mostly sprung from Nór's great-grandson Halfdan the Old
Yngling.fact: The 'genealogies' also claim that many heroic families famed in Scandinavian tradition but not in Norway were of a Finn-Kven stock, mostly sprung from Nór's great-grandson Halfdan the Old.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: Almost all the lineages sprung from _____ are then shown to reconvert in the person of Harald Fairhair, the first king of "all Norway"
Yngling.fact: The 'genealogies' also claim that many heroic families famed in Scandinavian tradition but not in Norway were of a Finn-Kven stock, mostly sprung from Nór's great-grandson Halfdan the Old. Almost all the lineages sprung from Halfdan are then shown to reconvert in the person of Harald Fairhair, the first king of "all Norway".

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: The 'Ættartölur' account ends to a genealogy of Harald's royal descendants down to Olaf IV of Norway with the statement that the account was written in _____, and with a list of the kings of Norway fr
Yngling.fact: The 'Ættartölur' account ends to a genealogy of Harald's royal descendants down to Olaf IV of Norway with the statement that the account was written in 1387, and with a list of the kings of Norway from this Olaf back to Harald Fair-hair.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: Another origin for the name skilfing is possible: _____ described Erik and Alrik, the sons of Skjalf to be the de facto ancestors of this Norse clan
Yngling.fact: Another origin for the name skilfing is possible: Snorri described Erik and Alrik, the sons of Skjalf to be the de facto ancestors of this Norse clan.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: A survivor _____ätälja was the ancestor of the Norwegian branch
Yngling.fact: A survivor Olof Trätälja was the ancestor of the Norwegian branch.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: Saxo on the _____ of Bråvalla (ca 750): Now the bravest of the Swedes were these: Arwakki, Keklu-Karl (Kelke-Karl), Krok the Peasant, (from Akr), Gudfast and Gummi from Gislamark
Yngling.fact: Saxo on the Battle of Bråvalla (ca 750): Now the bravest of the Swedes were these: Arwakki, Keklu-Karl (Kelke-Karl), Krok the Peasant, (from Akr), Gudfast and Gummi from Gislamark.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: These were kindred of the god _____, and most faithful witnesses to the gods
Yngling.fact: These were kindred of the god Frey, and most faithful witnesses to the gods. They likewise held the god Frey to be the founder of their race.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: They likewise held the god _____ to be the founder of their race
Yngling.fact: These were kindred of the god Frey, and most faithful witnesses to the gods. They likewise held the god Frey to be the founder of their race.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: Ingi (Yngwe) also, and Oly, Alver, Folki, all sons of Elrik (Alrek), embraced the service of _____; they were men ready of hand, quick in counsel, and very close friends of Ring
Yngling.fact: Ingi (Yngwe) also, and Oly, Alver, Folki, all sons of Elrik (Alrek), embraced the service of Sigurd Hring; they were men ready of hand, quick in counsel, and very close friends of Ring. Moreover, both in Icelandic sources and in the Gesta Danorum, King Sigurd Hring would become the ancestor of the houses of Ragnar Lodbrok and would thus be the semi-legendary ancestor of the House of Munsö through Björn Ironside, and the Danish royal house through Sigur.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: When the closing chapter maps out a full line, it diverges after _____
Yngling.fact: When the closing chapter maps out a full line, it diverges after Halfdan Hvitbeinn.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: The names of _____ kings are shown in bold
Yngling.fact: The names of Swedish kings are shown in bold. Likewise in the Skáldskaparmál the Scylfings are described as an eastern family and East King was a conventional kenning for a Swedish king.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: Likewise in the Skáldskaparmál the _____ are described as an eastern family and East King was a conventional kenning for a Swedish king
Yngling.fact: Likewise in the Skáldskaparmál the Scylfings are described as an eastern family and East King was a conventional kenning for a Swedish king.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: However, in the Ættartolur, (the genealogies attached to _____ byggdist), the Skilfings are of Norwegian origin and include a family identified as Skjöldungs
Yngling.fact: However, in the Ættartolur, (the genealogies attached to Hversu Noregr byggdist), the Skilfings are of Norwegian origin and include a family identified as Skjöldungs.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: In the eddic poem Grímnismál (stanza 55), _____ appears as one of Odin's names, the information there also appearing in the Gylfaginning.
Yngling.fact: There Skilfing (Skilfingr) appears as a synonym of Yngling, in a line on Egil, the father of Ottar, so that Ongentheow is considered identical to Egil. However, in the Ættartolur, (the genealogies attached to Hversu Noregr byggdist), the Skilfings are of Norwegian origin and include a family identified as Skjöldungs.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: For alliterative purposes the name could be extended, such as the form _____ 'Battle-Scylfing', which occurs once in the singular and twice in the plural
Yngling.fact: For alliterative purposes the name could be extended, such as the form Heathoscylfing 'Battle-Scylfing', which occurs once in the singular and twice in the plural.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: A _____ whose name is partly missing but ends in -ela married the sister of Hrothgar and Halga
Yngling.fact: For alliterative purposes the name could be extended, such as the form Heathoscylfing 'Battle-Scylfing', which occurs once in the singular and twice in the plural. A Scylfing whose name is partly missing but ends in -ela married the sister of Hrothgar and Halga.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: Specifically identified as _____ are Ongentheow, king of Sweden, and by extension his subject Wiglaf son of Weohstan
Yngling.fact: Specifically identified as Scylfings are Ongentheow, king of Sweden, and by extension his subject Wiglaf son of Weohstan. This literally means 'Scylfings'-helmet'; it is a kenning meaning both "ruler of the Scylfings" and "protector of the Scylfings".

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: This literally means '_____'-helmet'; it is a kenning meaning both "ruler of the Scylfings" and "protector of the Scylfings"
Yngling.fact: Specifically identified as Scylfings are Ongentheow, king of Sweden, and by extension his subject Wiglaf son of Weohstan. This literally means 'Scylfings'-helmet'; it is a kenning meaning both "ruler of the Scylfings" and "protector of the Scylfings".

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: Wiglaf and _____ belonged to the family of the Wægmundings to which Beowulf and his father Ecgtheow also belonged
Yngling.fact: Specifically identified as Scylfings are Ongentheow, king of Sweden, and by extension his subject Wiglaf son of Weohstan. Wiglaf and Weohstan belonged to the family of the Wægmundings to which Beowulf and his father Ecgtheow also belonged.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: Another extended form is helm _____
Yngling.fact: Another extended form is helm Scylfinga.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: The Beowulf poet uses it to refer to _____'s son Onela
Yngling.fact: The Beowulf poet uses it to refer to Ongentheow's son Onela.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: But neither _____ or Skjöldungs are specifically derived from these sons
Yngling.fact: But neither Skylfings or Skjöldungs are specifically derived from these sons.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: The fourth lineage is identified: One war-king was named _____; and his house is called the House of Skilfings: his kindred is in the Eastern Region
Yngling.fact: The fourth lineage is identified: One war-king was named Skelfir; and his house is called the House of Skilfings: his kindred is in the Eastern Region. In this list of the sons of Halfdan, Yngvi the ancestor of the Ynglings is missing and Skelfir the ancestor of the Skilfings appears in his place.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: A connection with the east might mean a connection to _____, but the vagueness of expression suggests Snorri knows no more about these Skilfings than he has written
Yngling.fact: A connection with the east might mean a connection to Sweden, but the vagueness of expression suggests Snorri knows no more about these Skilfings than he has written.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: Snorri also gives _____ as a kenning for "king" and it appears as a kenning for "sword" in the thulur found in some versions of the Skáldkskaparmál
Yngling.fact: The fourth lineage is identified: One war-king was named Skelfir; and his house is called the House of Skilfings: his kindred is in the Eastern Region. A connection with the east might mean a connection to Sweden, but the vagueness of expression suggests Snorri knows no more about these Skilfings than he has written.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: But nothing in the following genealogy is necessarily _____ though possible Swedish parallels do appear, particular the names Alrek and Eirík as discussed below
Yngling.fact: This might be a remembrance of an earlier identity or connection of the Swedish Ynglings and the Swedish Scylfings in Beowulf. But nothing in the following genealogy is necessarily Swedish though possible Swedish parallels do appear, particular the names Alrek and Eirík as discussed below.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: It claims _____ was king of Vörs (Vǫrs), modern Voss in northern Hordaland in southwestern Norway, but Halfdan's inheritance was in southeastern Norway
Yngling.fact: It claims Skelfir was king of Vörs (Vǫrs), modern Voss in northern Hordaland in southwestern Norway, but Halfdan's inheritance was in southeastern Norway. Skelfir was the father of Skjöld (Skjǫldr).

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: The account ends by saying that lineage of _____ was called the Skilfing lineage or the Skjöldung lineage, seemingly identifying the two
Yngling.fact: It claims Skelfir was king of Vörs (Vǫrs), modern Voss in northern Hordaland in southwestern Norway, but Halfdan's inheritance was in southeastern Norway. Skelfir was the father of Skjöld (Skjǫldr).

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: Indeed, the Ættartǫlur later twice gives a quite different list of descendants of the _____öld who is there made a son of Odin as commonly in Norse texts
Yngling.fact: Indeed, the Ættartǫlur later twice gives a quite different list of descendants of the Danish Skjöld who is there made a son of Odin as commonly in Norse texts.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: These two mentions are the only occurrences of Eirík the _____ in Norse texts
Yngling.fact: This Norwegian Skjöld, ancestor of the Norwegian Skjöldungs, is father of Eirík, father of Alrek (Alrekr), father of Eirík the Eloquent, whom the Skáldskaparmál presented as an Ylfing. These two mentions are the only occurrences of Eirík the Eloquent in Norse texts.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: But what seems to be the same figure appears prominently in book 5 of _____' Gesta Danorum as Ericus disertus
Yngling.fact: But what seems to be the same figure appears prominently in book 5 of Saxo Grammaticus' Gesta Danorum as Ericus disertus.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: This Ericus disertus is indeed a _____, but his father is not named Alrek but rather Regnerus pugilex, that is Ragnar the Champion
Yngling.fact: This Norwegian Skjöld, ancestor of the Norwegian Skjöldungs, is father of Eirík, father of Alrek (Alrekr), father of Eirík the Eloquent, whom the Skáldskaparmál presented as an Ylfing. This Ericus disertus is indeed a Norwegian, but his father is not named Alrek but rather Regnerus pugilex, that is Ragnar the Champion.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: Returning to the Ættartǫlur, there Eirík the _____ is father of Alrek, father of Víkar (Víkarr), father of Vatnar
Yngling.fact: Returning to the Ættartǫlur, there Eirík the Eloquent is father of Alrek, father of Víkar (Víkarr), father of Vatnar.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: This Víkar is the famous Víkar, king of Hördaland, who was sacrificed to Odin by _____
Yngling.fact: This Víkar is the famous Víkar, king of Hördaland, who was sacrificed to Odin by Starkad.

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: The chain of descent from Alrek to Víkar to _____ is also found in Hálfs saga ok Hálfsrekka ('The saga of Hálf and his heroes')
Yngling.fact: Returning to the Ættartǫlur, there Eirík the Eloquent is father of Alrek, father of Víkar (Víkarr), father of Vatnar. The chain of descent from Alrek to Víkar to Vatnar is also found in Hálfs saga ok Hálfsrekka ('The saga of Hálf and his heroes').

Yngling.subject: Important Days
Yngling.question: This genealogy may have been based on attempts to ascribe a Norwegian origin to both _____ and Danish Skjöldungs and also be related to Saxo's account of the Norwegian Ericus desertus
Yngling.fact: This genealogy may have been based on attempts to ascribe a Norwegian origin to both Swedish Scylfings and Danish Skjöldungs and also be related to Saxo's account of the Norwegian Ericus desertus.

Ynglinga saga.subject: Important Days
Ynglinga saga.question: Ynglinga saga (modern Icelandic pronunciation: [ˈiŋliŋka ˈsaːɣa]) is a Kings' saga, originally written in Old Norse by the Icelandic poet and historian Snorri Sturluson about _____
Ynglinga saga.fact: Ynglinga saga (modern Icelandic pronunciation: [ˈiŋliŋka ˈsaːɣa]) is a Kings' saga, originally written in Old Norse by the Icelandic poet and historian Snorri Sturluson about 1225.

Ynglinga saga.subject: Important Days
Ynglinga saga.question: It is the first section of his _____
Ynglinga saga.fact: It is the first section of his Heimskringla.

Ynglinga saga.subject: Important Days
Ynglinga saga.question: It was first translated into English and published in _____ by Samuel Laing
Ynglinga saga.fact: It was first translated into English and published in 1844 by Samuel Laing.

Ynglinga saga.subject: Important Days
Ynglinga saga.question: Snorri Sturluson based his work on an earlier _____ which is attributed to the Norwegian 9th-century skald Þjóðólfr of Hvinir, and which also appears in Historia Norwegiae
Ynglinga saga.fact: Snorri Sturluson based his work on an earlier Ynglingatal which is attributed to the Norwegian 9th-century skald Þjóðólfr of Hvinir, and which also appears in Historia Norwegiae.

Ynglinga saga.subject: Important Days
Ynglinga saga.question: It tells the most ancient part of the story of the House of _____ (Scylfings in Beowulf)
Ynglinga saga.fact: It tells the most ancient part of the story of the House of Ynglings (Scylfings in Beowulf).

Ynglinga saga.subject: Important Days
Ynglinga saga.question: Snorri described the descent of the kings of _____ from this royal house of Sweden
Ynglinga saga.fact: Snorri described the descent of the kings of Norway from this royal house of Sweden.

Ynglinga saga.subject: Important Days
Ynglinga saga.question: The saga deals with the arrival of the Norse gods to _____ and how Freyr founded the Swedish Yngling dynasty at Uppsala
Ynglinga saga.fact: The saga deals with the arrival of the Norse gods to Scandinavia and how Freyr set up the Swedish Yngling dynasty at Uppsala. The saga distinguishes between Swithiod the Great (literally "Sweden the Great"), where the opening scenes are set, and Sweden proper, in Scandinavia, where the reign of the Ynglings begins.

Ynglinga saga.subject: Important Days
Ynglinga saga.question: Then the saga follows the line of _____ kings until Ingjald (Ingjald illråde), after which the descendants settled in Norway and became the ancestors of the Norwegian King Harald Fairhair
Ynglinga saga.fact: The saga deals with the arrival of the Norse gods to Scandinavia and how Freyr set up the Swedish Yngling dynasty at Uppsala. Then the saga follows the line of Swedish kings until Ingjald (Ingjald illråde), after which the descendants settled in Norway and became the ancestors of the Norwegian King Harald Fairhair.

Ynglinga saga.subject: Important Days
Ynglinga saga.question: The Black Sea divides the earth into three parts: Asia in the east, Europe in the west and "_____ the Great, or the Cold" in the north
Ynglinga saga.fact: The Black Sea divides the earth into three parts: Asia in the east, Europe in the west and "Swithiod the Great, or the Cold" in the north. The saga distinguishes between Swithiod the Great (literally "Sweden the Great"), where the opening scenes are set, and Sweden proper, in Scandinavia, where the reign of the Ynglings begins.

Ynglinga saga.subject: Important Days
Ynglinga saga.question: The saga distinguishes between _____ the Great (literally "Sweden the Great"), where the opening scenes are set, and Sweden proper, in Scandinavia, where the reign of the Ynglings begins
Ynglinga saga.fact: The Black Sea divides the earth into three parts: Asia in the east, Europe in the west and "Swithiod the Great, or the Cold" in the north. The saga distinguishes between Swithiod the Great (literally "Sweden the Great"), where the opening scenes are set, and Sweden proper, in Scandinavia, where the reign of the Ynglings begins.

Ynglinga saga.subject: Important Days
Ynglinga saga.question: These lands differ in a metaphorical sense as well, since the former is also called _____ or the home of gods, while the latter is called Mannheim or the place where people live
Ynglinga saga.fact: These lands differ in a metaphorical sense as well, since the former is also called Godheim or the home of gods, while the latter is called Mannheim or the place where people live.

Ynglinga saga.subject: Important Days
Ynglinga saga.question: This mountain ridge (probably referring to the _____) lies "outside of all inhabited lands" but its southern part is not far from "Turkland" (probably Khazaria)
Ynglinga saga.fact: This mountain ridge (probably referring to the Ural Mountains) lies "outside of all inhabited lands" but its southern part is not far from "Turkland" (probably Khazaria).

Ynglinga saga.subject: Important Days
Ynglinga saga.question: On the southern side of the mountains runs the river Tanais, formerly known as _____ or Vanaquisl (the modern day Don), which flows into the Black Sea and marks the border between Europe and Asia
